clf-c02.focus: Shared responsibility, pricing, and core services

aif-c01.name: AI Practitioner
aif-c01.focus: Fundamentals of AI and generative AI, and responsible AI use

saa-c03.name: Solutions Architect – Associate
saa-c03.focus: Architecture design that meets availability, performance, and cost requirements

soa-c03.name: CloudOps Engineer
soa-c03.focus: Monitoring, incident response, reliability, and operational automation

dea-c01.name: Data Engineer
dea-c01.focus: Data ingestion, transformation, and pipeline operations

sap-c03.name: Solutions Architect – Professional
sap-c03.focus: Cross-organizational design, migration, and complex configurations

aip-c01.name: Generative AI Developer
aip-c01.focus: RAG, agents, and operating generative AI applications

scs-c03.name: Security
scs-c03.focus: Access control, data protection, and incident response

ai-business-strategist.name: AI Business Strategist
ai-business-strategist.focus: AI implementation decisions, governance, and business results

clf-c02.scope: Assesses your understanding of the value of the AWS Cloud, the shared responsibility model, the roles of key services, pricing, and support.
clf-c02.why: Focuses on basic terminology and how to properly use services.
clf-c02.audience: For people learning AWS for the first time, and for sales or planning staff who want to share the same cloud fundamentals with their development team.

aif-c01.scope: Covers the basics of AI, machine learning, and generative AI, the uses of foundation models, responsible AI, and data governance.
aif-c01.why: Being able to explain the uses and risks is more important than implementing a model.
aif-c01.audience: Those involved in planning and business improvement using AI, and those who have started learning AI development.

saa-c03.scope: Covers the design of AWS architectures that are secure, highly available, and meet performance and cost requirements.
saa-c03.why: Choose among similar architectures to meet constraints such as availability, connectivity, and operational overhead.
saa-c03.audience: Infrastructure engineers, SREs, and app developers who want to systematically learn AWS design.

dva-c03.scope: Handles application development on AWS, AI-assisted development, authentication and permissions, testing, deployment, and fault investigation.
dva-c03.why: Questions cover implementation behavior, such as Lambda retries and DynamoDB conditional updates.
dva-c03.audience: Developers building backend and serverless applications with AWS managed services.

soa-c03.scope: Covers AWS environment monitoring, reliability, failure response, networks, and operational automation.
soa-c03.why: Distinguish causes from symptoms and select a recovery or improvement method that fits the operational constraints.
soa-c03.audience: Cloud operations personnel and SREs who want to systematize monitoring and failure response.

dea-c01.scope: Covers data ingestion, transformation, storage, pipeline operations, and access management.
dea-c01.why: You need to understand the differences in latency, replay, cost, and access control for each processing method.
dea-c01.audience: Those involved in building and operating ETL, data lakes, and analysis platforms.

mla-c01.scope: Handles training data preparation, model development, deployment, and monitoring of models and infrastructure.
mla-c01.why: Questions cover both machine-learning evaluation metrics and deployment and operations on AWS.
mla-c01.audience: ML engineers who want to put trained models into production and continuously manage quality and costs.

sap-c03.scope: Covers cross-organizational cloud design, security and governance, cost, migration and business continuity, and operational automation. Designs that incorporate AI/ML are also included.
sap-c03.why: Simultaneously evaluate operations, costs, and recovery requirements when multiple accounts or existing-system constraints overlap.
sap-c03.audience: Architects reviewing designs across multiple teams, and tech leads responsible for cloud migration and standardization.

dop-c02.scope: Covers CI/CD, configuration management, monitoring, incident response, security and availability automation.
dop-c02.why: You need to design the full operational workflow, from deployments across multiple environments to rollbacks after an issue is detected.
dop-c02.audience: DevOps engineer and SRE responsible for automating release infrastructure and cloud operations for multiple teams.

aip-c01.scope: Covers the design, RAG, agents, evaluation, safety, and production operations of generative AI applications built with foundation models.
aip-c01.why: Consider retrieval and generation quality, access control, latency, and inference costs together.
aip-c01.audience: Developers and architects who take generative AI functions from verification to production.

scs-c03.scope: Covers identity and access management, encryption, infrastructure protection, threat detection, investigation and incident response.
scs-c03.why: Read the IAM, resource, and key policies across multiple accounts together to determine which actions are allowed or denied.
scs-c03.audience: Cloud security professionals responsible for security design, auditing, and vulnerability response.

ans-c01.scope: Covers AWS and on-premises connectivity, network design, route control, operations and troubleshooting.
ans-c01.why: Trace BGP routes, the direction of DNS forwarding, and reachability among multiple VPCs using the conditions given in the question.
ans-c01.audience: Those who design and operate hybrid infrastructure that uses Direct Connect and Transit Gateway.

ai-business-strategist.scope: Addresses AI investment prioritization, business value measurement, risk management, and organizational adoption and retention.
ai-business-strategist.why: In addition to understanding AI fundamentals, you need to compare business outcomes, implementation readiness, and governance for each case.
ai-business-strategist.audience: Business managers, product managers, and consultants responsible for decision-making on AI implementation.

glossary.definition: A method of controlling access by checking attributes such as tags attached to users and resources. Instead of duplicating a policy for each team, you can apply conditions that match team tags.

The four properties transactions should provide: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability. These matter when multiple updates must be applied together so that a failure midway does not leave only some of them committed.
AWS service that issues and manages TLS certificates. AWS-issued certificates linked to corresponding AWS services can be used for managed renewal if verification requirements are met.
A load balancer for HTTP and HTTPS requests. It is suited to routing requests by host name or URL path, unlike an NLB, which primarily handles TCP and UDP traffic.
Image used to launch an EC2 instance. You can recreate an instance with the OS and installed software.
An identifier for an AWS resource. It is used to specify resources in IAM policies; depending on the service, the region or account portion may be empty.
A group that manages the desired, minimum, and maximum number of EC2 instances, as well as their health.
Distinct locations within an AWS Region. To prepare for an AZ-level failure, consider distributing both compute and data across multiple AZs.
A way to run inference asynchronously on multiple inputs at once. For large workloads that do not need immediate results, compare it with continuously running real-time inference.
A protocol for exchanging routing information between networks. It is used with Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN when dynamic routing is supported.

A deployment method that runs the old and new environments in parallel, then switches traffic to the new environment after verification. Rollback is easier when data changes remain compatible with the old environment.

A deployment method that initially sends some traffic to the new version, checks metrics such as the error rate, and then gradually increases the share of traffic sent to it. This limits the impact of a problem.

A method for capturing changes such as inserts, updates, and deletes and continuously applying them to another system. Database migrations usually combine CDC with an initial load, and teams check for replication lag before cutover.
A method of expressing the network range using a prefix, such as 10.0.0.0/16. In designs that connect VPCs, overlapping ranges affect route selection.
A term formerly used in AWS KMS. The current general term is KMS key; keys created and managed by customers are called customer managed keys.

A mechanism in which the server uses HTTP headers to indicate the conditions under which resources from different origins can be used from the browser. Authentication and authorization for the resource itself is also applied separately.
A report that provides detailed information about AWS costs and usage. When analyzing costs by account or service, also check aggregation settings and whether cost allocation tags are enabled.
A queue that isolates messages that could not be processed or delivered. Decide which processing stages should send failures to it and how to address their causes before reprocessing the messages.
Design and procedures for recovering services and data in the event of a disaster. Determine RPO and RTO and verify actual switchover and cutback.
A feature that records item-level changes to a DynamoDB table in order. Downstream processes can be triggered by these changes, so they should be idempotent to handle retries.
Block storage used by EC2 and other services. Each volume belongs to an AZ; snapshots can be used to create a new volume in another AZ.
AWS orchestration service that manages container execution and service maintenance. The execution platform can be EC2 or AWS Fargate.
A managed service for running Kubernetes on AWS. It is an option when you need to retain Kubernetes APIs and existing operational assets.
A virtual network interface in a VPC. It belongs to a subnet; attaching a secondary ENI to another EC2 instance requires meeting conditions such as using the same AZ.
The process of extracting the original data, converting it, and then loading it to the storage destination. The order of processing is different from ELT, which performs conversion after loading.
A configuration that delivers one event to multiple subscribers. If each consumer needs independent processing throughput and retry behavior, consider a separate queue for each subscriber.

Controls that keep designs and operations within acceptable limits. In AWS Control Tower, these are now called controls and can prevent operations, detect violations, or inspect resources before creation.
A way to control access to AWS resources. Whether an action is allowed depends on the applicable identity-based and resource-based policies, as well as any permission limits that apply.
The property that repeating an equivalent request produces the same result and side effects as processing it once. Idempotency is essential for safely retrying orders and payments.

A gateway for communication between a VPC and the internet. For an EC2 instance to communicate directly over IPv4, it needs a public IPv4 address, a route through the gateway, and rules that allow the traffic.
A way to associate Kubernetes service accounts with IAM roles in EKS. Narrow the OIDC trust conditions and grant the target workloads only the permissions they need.

An AWS service for creating and managing cryptographic keys and controlling cryptographic operations. For cross-account access, check the key policy, the caller’s permissions, and any restrictions imposed by the target service.
The principle of granting identities only the permissions they need to perform their work. Limit the allowed actions, resources, and conditions of use.
Rules that control traffic at subnet boundaries. Because NACLs are stateless, required traffic must be allowed in both directions.
A mechanism for translating IP addresses in network packets. A public NAT Gateway is used for outbound IPv4 traffic from a private subnet to the internet.
A load balancer for TCP, UDP, TLS, and other traffic. It is suited to use cases that require a static IP address in each AZ; path-based HTTP routing is provided by ALB.
A mechanism by which CloudFront authenticates requests to supported origins such as S3. It prevents users from accessing the origin directly and limits delivery to CloudFront.
Authentication specification built on top of OAuth 2.0. When working with AWS, you can obtain temporary AWS credentials by validating the conditions of the token issued by the OIDC provider.
A unit that organizes accounts hierarchically in AWS Organizations. SCPs attached to OUs also apply to subordinate member accounts. IAM privileges are not granted just by belonging to an OU.

A disaster recovery approach that keeps only data and core components at the recovery site, then starts the full service after a disaster. Compared with warm standby, which keeps a reduced environment running, pilot light typically requires more recovery steps.

A feature for restoring data to a specified point in time within the retention period. Check each service’s retention limit, the latest restorable time, and whether restoration creates a new resource.

A way to connect privately to a service without routing traffic over the internet. It can avoid broad VPC-to-VPC connectivity and can be used in configurations where the connected VPCs have overlapping CIDR ranges.

A method that retrieves relevant documents and adds the retrieved content to the model’s input as context before generating an answer. Evaluate retrieval misses separately from cases where the model fails to use the retrieved content.
A policy in AWS Organizations that sets limits on the permissions that can be granted to supported resources. It complements an SCP, which sets limits on the principal side.

A target, expressed as a duration, for the maximum data loss acceptable during recovery. For example, an RPO of 5 minutes means that up to 5 minutes of data immediately before the failure may be lost.
The target time within which service must be restored after a failure. Account for restoration, restarts, DNS changes, and health checks.
A policy in AWS Organizations that sets the maximum permissions available to IAM principals in member accounts. An IAM policy or another permission-granting policy is still required to allow access.
A set of allow rules that controls traffic to and from resources in a VPC. Security groups are stateful, so response traffic for an allowed connection is permitted automatically.
An agreement between a service provider and a customer. It specifies service commitments such as availability, how they are measured, and what happens if the commitments are missed.
A measurement of service quality, such as the share of successful API requests or their response time. An SLI provides the measured value used to assess a service level objective (SLO).
A target for the quality of service provided to users. For example, define a 99.9% successful response rate over one month, along with the metric and scope of measurement.

glossary.expansion: Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys
glossary.definition: A way to encrypt stored data, such as S3 objects, on the service side, with AWS KMS managing the encryption keys. In addition to permission to perform operations on the objects, the corresponding KMS permissions are required.
A service that issues temporary security credentials for access to AWS. When assuming a role, check the role’s trust conditions and the caller’s permissions.
A service that connects multiple VPCs and on-premises networks through a central hub. Design route table associations and route propagation for each attachment.
The period for which data or a cached record is considered valid. DNS uses TTL for cache duration; DynamoDB TTL marks expired items for automatic deletion.
A logically isolated network in AWS. Define its IP ranges, subnets, routes, and connections, then design how public and private traffic flows.
A connection point in a VPC for reaching a service without routing traffic over the internet. Interface endpoints use ENIs and DNS; gateway endpoints use route table entries for supported services.
A way to allow, block, or count HTTP requests based on defined conditions. AWS WAF is associated with supported services such as CloudFront and ALB.

A disaster recovery approach that keeps a reduced but functioning version of the system running at the recovery site and scales it up after a failure. Compare it with pilot light in terms of cost and failover time.
A service for launching virtual servers on demand. Use it when you need to manage the operating system and runtime environment; an AMI can be used to create instances with the same configuration.
A service that runs code in response to events. AWS manages the underlying servers, and events such as an object being stored in S3 or a message arriving in SQS can trigger processing.
A service that stores objects in a bucket. Unlike EFS for file sharing and EBS, which handles in blocks, objects are read and written using an API.
NFS file storage that can be shared by multiple computing environments. Used for reading and writing common files in Linux applications.
A family of services that provides managed file systems such as Windows File Server and Lustre. Choose a file system based on the protocols and features your application requires.
A service that manages tasks such as relational database setup and backups. Consider it when you need SQL or transactions, and compare it with non-relational databases such as DynamoDB.
A relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL. Its compute and storage are separated, making it an option when considering high availability or read scaling.
A serverless database for key-value and document data. Access patterns, including the choice of partition key, are important; it is not designed around arbitrary joins as in RDS.
A managed in-memory caching service. It can cache frequently accessed data to reduce database load and response times.
A content delivery network (CDN) that serves content from edge locations. Caching content closer to users reduces load on the origin and delivery latency.
A service for DNS resolution, domain registration, and health checks. It maps names to destinations and can use routing policies to control which destination is returned.
A service that publishes and manages APIs. Set up authentication and throttling, and connect requests to backends such as Lambda.
A service that receives events from services and applications and delivers them to destinations that match the rules. Used to separate the event source and processing destination.
A service that delivers messages to multiple destinations that subscribe to a topic. Fan-out configuration allows the same event to be delivered to multiple SQS queues.

A service that stores messages in queues until consumers retrieve them. It decouples producers from consumers and absorbs fluctuations in load. Design for idempotent processing in case messages are delivered more than once.
A workflow service that connects multiple steps using a state machine. Define branches, parallel execution, and retries to orchestrate tasks such as Lambda functions.
A service that monitors systems by collecting metrics, logs, and other data. Alarms can detect anomalies and trigger operational responses.
A service that records user and service actions in AWS as events. Use it to investigate who called which API; unlike CloudWatch, it records API activity rather than monitoring system performance.
A service that records AWS resource configurations and their change history. It evaluates configuration compliance against rules and helps investigate unintended changes.

A service that defines AWS resource configurations in templates and creates or updates resources as stacks. It helps reduce inconsistencies from manual configuration and lets you manage environment configurations as code.
A service for centrally managing multiple AWS accounts. Organize accounts into OUs and apply organization-wide controls using policies such as SCPs.
A service for setting up and controlling AWS environments with multiple accounts. Use landing zones and controls to help standardize account management.
A service that stores secrets such as passwords and API keys, helping you avoid embedding credentials in code. It supports rotation when the appropriate integrations are configured.
A service that provides application user registration and sign-in. Its use differs from IAM Identity Center, which manages employee access to AWS accounts and applications.
A service that protects applications from DDoS attacks. It complements WAF, which inspects HTTP requests against rules.
A service that helps discover sensitive data in S3. It can identify where data such as personal information is stored and support data protection investigations and responses.
A service that analyzes logs, events, and other data to detect threats. It reports findings such as suspicious access and provides leads for security investigations.

glossary.expansion: AWS Security Hub Cloud Security Posture Management
glossary.definition: A service that evaluates AWS security settings against standards and aggregates findings. It continuously checks for resource misconfigurations and compliance.
A service that centralizes authentication and access management for employees using multiple AWS accounts and applications. Permission sets assign account access.

A pricing model that discounts eligible compute usage in exchange for a commitment to a specified spend per hour for a set term. Coverage depends on the plan type, and the model is distinct from capacity reservations.

A pricing option for EC2 and other services that offers discounts in exchange for a commitment to specified conditions and a term. For EC2, regional and zonal scopes differ in whether capacity is reserved.
A way to use unused EC2 capacity at a discount. Because instances can be interrupted, consider Spot for retryable batch or distributed workloads.
A managed service for building generative AI applications with foundation models. In addition to invoking models, it can be used with RAG, Bedrock Guardrails, and other features.
A service that supports building, training, and deploying machine learning models. It covers workflows such as training a model on your own data and using it through inference endpoints.
A unit used by generative AI models to process text. Text is split into tokens that may be whole words, parts of words, or symbols; the token count for the same text varies by model and language.
A numerical vector representation of the meaning or features of text and other data. Similarity between vectors can be used to find related information, including in the retrieval step of RAG.

A way to adapt a pretrained model using additional training data. It updates the model’s weights to suit a specific task or response format. Its purpose and mechanism differ from RAG, which retrieves external information.

A phenomenon in which generative AI produces plausible-sounding content that is unsupported or factually incorrect. RAG can provide supporting information but cannot eliminate hallucinations, so sources still need to be checked and outputs evaluated.

An attack that embeds malicious instructions in user input or retrieved documents to make a generative AI system act against its intended instructions. Systems should be designed not to treat external content as instructions.
A database that stores vectors such as embeddings and supports similarity search. It can find semantically related information that an exact keyword match may miss.
A service that helps build data lakes and manage access to them. It works with the data catalog to manage fine-grained permissions for tables and other resources.
A data integration service for discovering, cataloging, and transforming data. ETL jobs can prepare data from multiple sources in formats suited to analysis.
A service that ingests continuously generated data as streams and lets multiple applications process it. It is used for low-latency processing of logs, events, and similar data.

A feature that evaluates generative-AI inputs and model responses to detect and control harmful content and confidential information. You can define policies for topics and information that should not be handled; these are separate from Control Tower controls.
Using computing, storage, and networking resources over a network as needed, then adjusting them to demand.
Requesting and using resources when needed instead of preparing all capacity in advance.
Pricing based on usage factors such as time, stored data, or requests; costs must be checked per resource.
The ability to increase or decrease capacity for changing load; it is separate from fault isolation.
Increasing capacity by adding workers or instances; placement still matters for availability.
Reducing the number of workers or instances while confirming remaining capacity is sufficient.
Increasing the capacity of one compute resource, unlike scaling out by adding instances.
A model that separates AWS and customer responsibilities; the boundary varies by service.
A geographic area for AWS resources; changing the selected Region does not move existing resources.
Designing to separate the scope affected by one failure; adding capacity alone does not provide it.
The property of a service being usable when needed, set according to outage impact and tolerable time.
Storage that keeps data as objects accessed through APIs, rather than as a directly mounted OS directory.
A logical container for S3 objects, which are addressed by keys within the bucket.
The name that identifies an object in an S3 bucket, supplied to APIs rather than treated as a file-system path.
Storage attached as a disk to compute, suited to file systems and continuous database reads and writes.
A software-provided server environment; with EC2 instances, the customer manages the OS, applications, and updates.
Running code with execution configuration instead of continuously managing server counts; it does not mean servers do not exist.
A design that starts processing in response to events such as file arrival or an API call.
A database type that works with business data through related tables, SQL, and transactions.
A broad term for databases that use a nonrelational data model. For a key-value database such as DynamoDB, start by designing access patterns, including which keys you will use to read data.
A language for defining, querying, and updating relational data; knowing it alone does not select a service.
The way data is read and written by key or condition; DynamoDB design starts with it.
Verifying the identity of a principal attempting access; it is separate from authorization.
Deciding which actions an authenticated principal may perform on which resources.
An entity able to perform AWS actions, such as an IAM user, role, AWS service, or federated user.
An identity with permission policies that a principal assumes to use temporary credentials.
Dynamically created credentials with an expiration, used with roles or federation to reduce long-term key distribution.
A document defining actions a principal may perform on resources; evaluate who, action, and resource.
A denial stated in policy that takes precedence over Allow during IAM evaluation.
Encryption that protects data moving between a client and service; HTTPS protects HTTP with TLS.
Encryption protecting stored data such as disks, databases, and objects; it is separate from TLS in transit.
A security protocol providing peer authentication, confidentiality of communication contents, and integrity against modification.
A policy controlling access to a KMS key; check KMS permissions separately from data-read permission.
Keeping data or resources from a point in time for recovery; job success alone does not prove restoration works.
Returning a recovery point to a target and confirming the application can use it; define target and procedure in advance.
Regularly evaluating whether backups can actually be restored, preferably in an isolated destination.
A value such as a password, API key, or token that must not be exposed in code, configuration, chat, or logs.
Updating a secret and ensuring its consumers follow the new value; storage alone is not enough.

glossary.expansion: Continuous integration and continuous delivery or deployment
glossary.definition: A development practice that repeatedly integrates, builds, tests, and releases changes. CI checks frequent integrations, and CD automates the steps that deliver verified changes to production.
Keeps verified changes ready for production release. Approval or an operational rule can determine when a release proceeds.
Automatically deploys changes to production after they pass the required checks. Monitoring and rollback preparation are part of the process.
A file or container image produced by a pipeline step and consumed by another. Identifying the verified artifact allows the same build to reach production.
An AWS service that defines and runs software release workflows. It connects steps such as source retrieval, build, test, approval, and deployment.
A pass condition for moving a change to the next stage. For example, the release stops if a required test fails.
A test that feeds input to a small unit such as a function and checks its output or state change. It helps isolate a failure.
A test that combines components or services to verify behavior across boundaries, such as data formats, authentication, or communication.
A test that starts at a user-facing entry point and checks whether the full workflow produces the intended result.
A test that detects whether an earlier defect has returned or a change has broken existing behavior.
Replaces running instances or tasks with the new version in groups. Keep versions compatible and maintain enough capacity while both run.
Restores a known working state after a problematic change. When redirecting traffic to the earlier version, check whether the newer version changed shared data.
Recovers by deploying a new version with a fix. It is an option when a data change has already made the old version incompatible.
An AWS service that automates application deployments. Depending on the configuration, it can redeploy the last known successful revision after a failure.
A numerical measure of changing conditions, such as request counts or response times. CloudWatch aggregates observations recorded with timestamps.
A record of an event with information such as its time or identifier. Logs help explain an error or show what happened during a particular request.
Records the path of a request across services, including operation order and duration. It helps locate slow calls.
Measures elapsed time, for example from sending a request to receiving the response. Compare measurements for the same operation with the same start and end points.
A value at or below which about 95% of measurements fall. A response-time p95 of 400 ms means that about 95% of the measured requests received a response within 400 ms.
The interval over which SLO attainment is evaluated. It may follow fixed calendar boundaries, such as a month, or roll forward, such as the past 28 days.
A condition in which no value arrives for an expected interval. Check other metrics or logs to distinguish no requests from failed collection.
Keeps database connections open so applications can reuse them. If none is available, a request may have to wait for a connection to be returned.
A service that accepts application connections to Amazon RDS and uses a connection pool to reuse database connections across those clients.
A DNS record that maps a domain name to an IPv4 address.
A DNS record that maps a domain name to an IPv6 address.
A name server that maintains a zone's DNS records and returns authoritative answers.
The first four and last IPv4 addresses in each AWS subnet, reserved by AWS and unavailable for resource assignment.
A DNS record that makes one DNS name an alias for another canonical DNS name.
A route for all destinations when no more-specific route matches, commonly 0.0.0.0/0 for IPv4.
A distributed naming system that maps domain names to information such as IP addresses.
The mechanism by which a parent zone uses NS records to direct queries to a child zone's authoritative name servers.
An item in a DNS zone that associates a name with information such as an IP address or delegation target.
A component that receives a client's name query, consults DNS servers as needed, and returns a result.
A portion of the DNS namespace and its records managed as one administrative unit by authoritative name servers.
A static public IPv4 address allocated to an AWS account that can be remapped to a supported resource.
A port number temporarily selected by a client or similar host as a communication source, relevant to return traffic rules.
An application-layer protocol in which clients and servers exchange requests, responses, methods, and status codes.
A three-digit code in an HTTP response that indicates the result of processing a request, such as 404.
HTTP carried over TLS to protect the communication channel; it does not change HTTP request and response semantics.
An address that identifies a host or network interface as a destination on an IP network.
The Internet Protocol version using 32-bit addresses, used by CIDR notation and A records.
The Internet Protocol version using 128-bit addresses, mapped in DNS with AAAA records.
A route that AWS adds to a route table to keep traffic for a VPC CIDR range within that VPC.
The rule that selects the route with the longest prefix, or most-specific CIDR, when multiple routes match a destination IP.
A DNS record that identifies authoritative name servers for a zone and is used for DNS delegation.
A bounded unit of network communication containing control information and data.
A 16-bit number that distinguishes a destination or source application on an IP address.
The number of leading bits fixed as the network portion in CIDR notation; a larger value makes an IPv4 range smaller.
An AWS subnet associated with a route table that has no direct route to an internet gateway.
An IPv4 address usable as a destination on the internet; in AWS it combines with an IGW route for internet reachability.
An AWS subnet associated with a route table that has a route to an internet gateway.
Routing information that maps a destination CIDR to a next hop and determines where packets are sent.
A collection of routes that pairs destination CIDRs with route targets for traffic leaving a subnet or similar scope.
The forwarding destination paired with a destination CIDR in a route table, such as an IGW, NAT gateway, or VPC peering connection.
An IP address range carved from a VPC CIDR range and created in one Availability Zone.
A transport protocol that establishes connections and provides a reliable ordered byte stream through sequencing and retransmission.
The message exchange at the start of a TLS connection that authenticates peers and agrees cryptographic parameters and keys.
A datagram transport protocol that does not itself provide connection establishment, ordering, or retransmission.
A connection that enables communication using private IP addresses between two VPCs and requires routes on both sides.
A mechanism that creates an encrypted tunnel across a network such as the internet to connect networks.
An automated sequence that moves a change through stages such as build, test, approval, and deployment, stopping later stages on failure.
The process of producing a runnable or distributable package or container image from source code and dependencies.
Advancing the same tested artifact to a later environment, such as from staging to production, without rebuilding it.
An immutable identifier calculated from content, used to identify and promote the exact tested image or artifact.
An environment or stage for validating a candidate artifact and configuration before production.
A fully managed build service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces deployable artifacts.
Managed fixed input, prerequisite data, or configuration used to establish reproducible test conditions.
A simulated implementation or response used in place of an external dependency during testing; it is distinct from validating real boundaries in integration or E2E tests.
Configuration that enables or disables a feature without redeploying code; it can limit impact during an incident but requires managed defaults and changes.
A check that determines whether an application or target is able to serve requests; failure can be a condition to halt or roll back deployment.
The controlled movement of data or schema to a new format or location, designed with old/new application compatibility, recovery, and data-loss handling.
The volume or flow of requests reaching a system; gradual deployments control the share sent to a new version and observe load and user impact.
The proportion of in-scope requests defined as failures, with numerator, denominator, operation, and observation window stated for decisions such as deployment aborts.
A view of how much processing capacity or resource is consumed and how much headroom remains, interpreted with measures such as CPU, queues, and request volume.
A boundary value for a measurement that triggers an action such as alerting, stopping, or expansion; define the metric, evaluation period, comparison, and response beforehand.
A periodic signal showing that a collector or process is operating, used to help distinguish no requests from missing measurement.
The ability to explain system state from observations such as metrics, logs, and traces, then choose the next hypothesis or action to investigate.
A common set of observation perspectives—latency, errors, traffic, and saturation—used together to distinguish user impact, load, and capacity headroom.
One measurement associated with a specific time or period; interpret it with its target, unit, timestamp, and aggregation period.
The process of delivering an application revision and configuration to a target environment so it can serve users, together with strategy, monitoring, and recovery.
The property that old and new applications, APIs, or data formats can operate correctly together; gradual delivery separates destructive changes into later steps.
Authentication using more than one factor; it strengthens identity verification but does not grant authorization.
A service where AWS manages parts of the underlying infrastructure; customer configuration responsibilities remain.
A mechanism that lets identities authenticated by an external provider use temporary AWS credentials.
An encryption key managed in AWS KMS; the current term is AWS KMS key, replacing the former CMK terminology.
A primary-key element that determines item placement and lookup in DynamoDB; choose it from access patterns.
A unit that treats multiple reads or writes as one operation, avoiding partial updates on failure.
A deployment across multiple Availability Zones to reduce a single-AZ failure scope; routing and data access still need design.
Credentials represented by access keys without an expiration; avoid embedding them and prefer temporary credentials where possible.
A backed-up data or resource state used for restoration; it is the point in time selected for recovery.
A managed policy that sets the maximum permissions an IAM principal can receive; it does not grant permissions itself.
A policy attached directly to a resource that allows or denies actions for principals; evaluate it with other applicable policies.
A request from an application to a service according to an API definition; it can be an event that invokes Lambda.
A practice of merging changes into a shared branch frequently and building and testing every change to catch problems early.
A resolver that answers DNS queries from resources in a VPC. It can resolve public records, VPC-specific names, and names in associated private hosted zones.
An AWS service for collecting, retaining, and searching logs from applications and AWS services. It can find records associated with an error or request ID.
An AWS service that collects request traces and helps inspect application paths and the duration of individual calls.
A managed service that translates addresses for connections initiated by VPC resources. A public NAT gateway can provide internet access from a private subnet.
A VPC endpoint for accessing S3 or DynamoDB in the same Region without an internet gateway. A route for the service is added to each selected route table.
A set of one or more CIDR blocks. In a VPC, route tables and security group rules can reference the set instead of listing each block separately.
An address assigned to a VPC resource from its subnet's IPv4 range. It can be used within connected networks and is not directly reachable from the public internet.
A field listing identifiers in a TLS certificate. For HTTPS, the client checks the requested host name against the DNS names in the SAN.
The sequence from a server certificate through any intermediate certificates to a root trusted by the client. The client verifies the signatures along this path.

glossary.expansion: Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys
glossary.definition: Server-side encryption that Amazon S3 performs with Amazon S3 managed keys; it is the default encryption for new S3 objects.
Base software that manages hardware resources and runs applications. On EC2, the customer manages the guest operating system configuration and updates.
The operating system running inside a virtual machine. For EC2, the customer manages its patches and configuration separately from AWS physical infrastructure.
A protocol for secure remote login and services over an insecure network. A working SSH connection does not prove that HTTPS on another port works.
The processor that executes instructions. CPU utilization is a load signal, but concurrent errors do not by themselves prove that CPU is the cause.
A text format for tabular data with values separated by commas. During ingestion, validate its contents separately from retaining the original file.
A system for storing, retrieving, and updating data. Choose a type such as relational or NoSQL and its access pattern for the workload.
A value that identifies one request. Recording it in logs and traces lets you correlate different observations about that request.
Measuring system state to detect anomalies, investigate causes, and check changes. Missing data must distinguish no requests from stopped measurement.
A notification that a state needs human attention. Define its recipient, condition, and the checks and next action it triggers.
A CloudWatch rule that evaluates metrics against a threshold over evaluation periods and can notify or act on state changes. It can support a deployment stop decision.
A Route 53-specific DNS record that routes a name to a supported AWS resource. It resembles CNAME but can be created at the root domain.
A Route 53 container for a domain and its DNS records. A public hosted zone serves public DNS; a private hosted zone resolves names within associated VPCs.
A rule that determines which record value Route 53 returns for a DNS query. It selects DNS answers and does not guarantee full application health.
A certificate that binds a server name to a public key in TLS. The client verifies the name, validity period, and trust chain to identify the peer.
Changing where user requests go, from an old version to a new one or back, gradually or at once. It is distinct from replacing tasks and is governed by observations and abort conditions.
An Amazon S3 feature that sends notification of events such as object creation to Lambda, SQS, SNS, or EventBridge, allowing the receiver to start processing.
A resource-based policy that specifies which principals and conditions may assume an IAM role. It differs from the permissions policy that specifies what the role may do.
An Amazon RDS Proxy metric that measures the time to borrow a database connection in microseconds. Compare it separately from SQL execution time and full API latency.
A short time span within the full interval of a period-based SLO. For example, divide a day into one-minute periods and check whether the indicator meets the threshold in each.
A Route 53 hosted zone for DNS records that resolvers on the internet can query. It can point a public name such as example.com to the website that serves it.
A Route 53 hosted zone for DNS records used by associated VPCs and configured private environments. It can resolve an internal API name to a private IP address.
The top-level name of a DNS zone, such as example.com in the example.com zone. A CNAME is unavailable there, but a Route 53 alias can point it to a supported AWS resource.
A policy on a supported VPC endpoint that controls which principals can perform which actions on which resources through it. The caller’s policies and resource policies also affect access.
Filtering that remembers connection state. A VPC security group automatically allows return traffic for an allowed connection.
Filtering that evaluates traffic without remembering connection state. A VPC network ACL must allow both the request and the return traffic in their respective directions.
A DNS record that holds text, often for domain verification or an SPF policy that identifies authorized mail senders.
A DNS record naming a server that accepts email for a domain and giving it a priority. Senders normally try the server with the lowest priority value first.
A DNS record that specifies which certificate authorities may issue TLS certificates for a domain. The issuing authority checks this record.
A policy attached to an IAM user, group, or role that defines which actions that identity can perform and under what conditions.
The IAM policy element that identifies the actions covered by a statement. For example, s3:GetObject reads an S3 object.
The IAM policy element that specifies when a statement applies. For example, it can check whether a request comes from a specified IP range.
A way to allow a named principal to perform specific operations with one KMS key. A grant can be created and later revoked without editing the key policy.
Analysis of source code or configuration without running the program. A linter can flag rule violations and code patterns likely to cause problems.
The build specification for AWS CodeBuild, written in YAML. It can specify when to run commands and where to find reports and artifacts.

An HTTP status code in the 500 range indicating that a server could not handle a request. During investigation, distinguish errors returned by the load balancer from errors returned by the application.
An error code indicating that the requested operation was denied. In Amazon S3, check the requested operation, the target resource, and the policies that apply.
An API operation that retrieves an object from an Amazon S3 bucket by key. In an IAM policy, s3:GetObject grants the basic permission for this operation.
An API operation that stores an object under a specified key in an Amazon S3 bucket. In an IAM policy, s3:PutObject grants the basic permission for this operation.
AWS guidance for designing and operating systems. Use it to review design decisions from perspectives such as security, reliability, and cost, and identify opportunities for improvement.
An open-source relational database that stores data in tables and supports querying and updating with SQL. It is also available on Amazon RDS.

A library for Java applications that keeps database connections open for reuse. maximumPoolSize sets the maximum number of connections, and connectionTimeout sets the maximum time to wait for an available connection.
A CloudWatch metric showing the number of network connections from clients connected to an Amazon RDS DB instance. It reports the instance-wide value; connections by DB user are counted separately.
A view for examining each PostgreSQL server process, including its connected user and execution state. Filtering by the application’s DB user lets you verify that application’s connections.
A CloudWatch metric showing the number of HTTP 5xx responses returned by the Application Load Balancer itself. 5xx responses returned by the target application are reported by a different metric.
The ability to increase or decrease computing resources as demand or usage changes. It helps increase capacity only during peak ordering periods and restore it when demand subsides.
An AWS service that adjusts the number of Amazon EC2 instances based on demand or a schedule. It monitors instance health and can replace unhealthy instances.
A pillar for establishing procedures and decision criteria and continuously improving system operations. For example, automate routine tasks and incorporate lessons from incidents into procedures.
A pillar for protecting data and systems. It restricts permissions to what is necessary, encrypts data, and establishes capabilities to detect and respond to anomalies.

The ability to continue required processing under expected conditions and recover when failures occur. In AWS Well-Architected, the scope of failure impacts and recovery methods are considered from the design stage.
A pillar for selecting resources that meet workload performance requirements and reviewing them as requirements and technologies change. Measure load and determine resource types and sizes.
A pillar for controlling cloud spending while meeting required functionality and quality. Measure usage by service and review unnecessary resources and pricing models that are no longer suitable.
A pillar for reducing a workload’s environmental impact. Review the workload so required processing uses fewer resources, such as by reducing underutilized resources.

A framework for organizing the preparation needed for cloud adoption across six perspectives: business, people, governance, platform, security, and operations. For example, plan staff development and an operating model alongside migration.
Measuring usage of CPU, memory, and other resources, then selecting resource types and sizes that better fit the workload. Check performance requirements during normal operation and at peak times.
A method of using software licenses already owned in the cloud. The product’s contract terms determine which services and host types can be used.

The mechanism that determines whether an AWS request is allowed. It checks the requester, action, resource, conditions, and applicable policies. An applicable explicit deny takes precedence over an allow.
A browser-based interface for configuring and managing AWS services. The operations you can view or perform depend on the account you use and your IAM permissions.
A command-line tool for operating AWS services from a terminal. It can be used in scripts that repeat the same operations and in automation workflows.
Language-specific libraries for calling AWS services from application code. They handle request signing and retries based on configuration, among other tasks.
A service for accessing AWS audit reports, compliance-related documents, and applicable agreements. Your own resource configurations and operation history must be recorded separately.

A service that scans supported EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions to detect software vulnerabilities and other issues. Use the findings to investigate impact and prioritize remediation.
An attack that concentrates traffic or requests from many distributed sources, preventing legitimate users from using a service. In AWS, protections such as AWS Shield can be used.

The user created when an AWS account is created, with permissions over the entire account. Protect it with multi-factor authentication, and use separate credentials with only the permissions needed for routine administration.
An IAM role that users or systems in another AWS account can assume. The role's trust policy specifies who can assume it, while its permissions policy specifies what can be done after it is assumed.
Storage that organizes files into directories and accesses them by specifying file names and paths. In AWS, files shared by multiple execution environments can be stored in Amazon EFS.
The storage category specified for an Amazon S3 object. Choose one based on access frequency, required retrieval time, retention period, and availability requirements.
A service that connects an on-premises network to AWS through an IPsec-encrypted tunnel. For example, it can connect an internal network to applications in a VPC.

A service that provides a dedicated network connection from an on-premises environment or similar location to AWS through a Direct Connect location. Bandwidth, redundancy, and communication encryption are designed to meet your requirements.

A method of defining configurations such as networks and servers in code, so changes can be tracked and configurations reproduced. In AWS, configurations can be defined with CloudFormation templates and similar tools.

A set of features for reviewing AWS invoices and payment information, analyzing costs and usage, managing budgets, and optimizing spending. For example, you can configure invoice-detail reviews and budget-overrun notifications for different purposes.
Tags used to aggregate AWS costs and usage by project, department, or other dimensions. In addition to tagging resources, you enable the tags used for aggregation in billing management.

A feature that classifies AWS costs into business units such as departments and products based on accounts, services, cost allocation tags, and other conditions. Because classification is rule-based, expenses across multiple accounts can be consolidated.
A mechanism in which the AWS Organizations management account receives a consolidated bill for the organization and makes the payment. Costs for member accounts can still be reviewed individually.
A tool for estimating costs by entering the AWS services you plan to use and their expected usage. It is useful for comparing architectures and setting a budget before adoption.

A feature for viewing AWS costs and usage broken down by service, account, period, and other dimensions. For example, you can use it to investigate services whose spending increased compared with the previous month.

A feature that sets budgets for AWS spending or usage and notifies designated owners when actual or forecasted values exceed thresholds. You should also define who checks what after a notification and operate accordingly.

An EC2 purchase option in which you pay for what you use, without a long-term contract or upfront usage commitment. It is also suitable for workloads whose duration or required instance count is difficult to predict.
An option that lets you run EC2 instances on a single dedicated physical server. You can control instance placement on the host and consider using licenses based on physical cores or other criteria.
EC2 instances that run on dedicated hardware isolated from instances belonging to other AWS accounts. You cannot specify the physical host where the instances are placed.

A feature that reserves capacity for EC2 instances with specified attributes in a specific Availability Zone. Capacity is reserved in advance so the desired number of instances can be launched when needed.
Charges incurred based on the data transfer path and amount. Check the pricing terms for the services you use, including transfers to the internet and communication across Regions.
A service that provides assistance with AWS accounts, billing, and technical issues. The scope of technical support and response terms vary by the plan you subscribe to.
Usage limits for AWS services that apply by account, Region, or other scope. For adjustable limits, you can request an increase through the Service Quotas console or other means.
A feature that checks the status of AWS resources from cost, security, performance, and other perspectives and suggests improvements. Available checks vary by support plan and other factors.
A dashboard where you can view the operating status of AWS services overall and events affecting your account. You can investigate the impact of outages and check scheduled maintenance.
An AWS catalog where you can search for and procure software, data, and services offered by third parties. Before deployment, confirm the pricing model, licensing, and operational responsibilities.
A community where AWS users and experts can ask and answer questions and search for Knowledge Center articles. Verify that any procedures you find apply to the services or features you use.
A broad term for technologies that use computers to support human intellectual tasks such as learning, reasoning, and recognition. It includes machine learning and generative AI.
A method that trains models on patterns in data and uses them to classify new data or predict numerical values. For example, it can learn characteristics of fraudulent transactions from past orders.

A method of training a model with data pairs consisting of inputs and their corresponding correct answers. For example, a model can be built to classify new transactions using the correct fraud determinations for individual transactions as training answers.
A method of finding structure in data without correct-answer labels. For example, customers with similar usage patterns can be grouped together.

A method that learns a policy to maximize rewards by using actions taken in a given state and the rewards obtained as a result. The design of the environment and rewards affects which actions are learned.
A correct answer or category name attached to data. For example, if an image is a receipt, the label “receipt” can be attached and used as a correct example in supervised learning.
A task that assigns inputs to predefined categories. For example, it can determine whether a new order is more like a normal transaction or one that requires review.
A task that predicts a continuous numerical value from input. For example, it can estimate a product’s price or the time until roadside assistance arrives.

The process of providing input to a trained model and obtaining a result such as a classification, prediction, or generation. The execution method is chosen based on whether an immediate response is needed or the work can be processed in batches over time.
An inference method that returns a result each time it receives input. It is used when the delay from request to response matters, such as returning a judgment while someone is operating a screen.
A method that completes inference after accepting input, with the result retrieved later. It is used for tasks such as image analysis, where users do not need to wait for the result immediately.

A method that returns generated results as they become available. In a conversational interface, users can see the response from its opening sentences without waiting for the entire response to be completed.

A problem in which input patterns or the relationship between inputs and results change during operation, making the model less suitable for its purpose than it was during training. Monitor and investigate inputs, outputs, and outcomes that become known later.
An AWS service that converts speech to text. For example, it can transcribe recorded inquiries so their content can be reviewed or searched.
An AWS service that translates text into another supported language. For example, an application can request a translation of an inquiry.
An AWS service that detects language, entities, sentiment, and other information in text. For example, it can extract product names from inquiry text to analyze trends.
An AWS service for building bots that interact with users through speech or text. For example, a bot can determine the intent to make a reservation and collect the required date and number of people.
An AWS service that converts text into synthesized speech. For example, applications can use it to read announcements or articles aloud.
AI that generates text, images, code, and other content from instructions or input. Because its output may contain errors, review it for the intended use before publishing or executing it.

A model pretrained on large datasets that can be adapted to multiple uses, such as text generation, summarization, and classification. The supported inputs, generatable formats, and costs vary by model.
Instructions or information provided to generative AI. Specify concretely what it should do, which information it may reference, and the required output format.
The range of context a model can handle in a single inference. Its length is measured in tokens, so check the limit when including conversation history or text retrieved through search.
An AI application that decides what to do next based on a goal, uses authorized tools, and checks the results. Set authorization and approval requirements for external actions.
People supervising decisions or operations assisted by AI. For important answers or money transfers, responsible staff can review and approve the proposed action.
The practice of adjusting the instructions, examples, context, and constraints given to generative AI to obtain responses suited to a goal. Compare results using representative inputs.

A method of showing a small number of input-output examples in a prompt to communicate the expected classification or answer format to a model. It helps verify how clearly instructions work without retraining the model.
A feature in Amazon Bedrock for creating reusable prompts and managing templates and versions. Evaluate prompts according to their use and changes, then decide which to adopt.
A method of training a pre-trained model further on domain-specific data. Consider it when adapting the model to specialized terminology and writing patterns.

A method of teaching one model specific behavior using responses and other outputs from a teacher model. Evaluate whether inference costs can be reduced while maintaining the quality required for the use case.
The proportion of all classified cases for which the prediction matches the correct answer. When the target class is rare, such as fraudulent transactions, also check recall and other metrics.

The proportion of cases that were actually positive among those the model classified as positive. In fraud detection, this evaluates how many legitimate transactions are mixed in with transactions classified as fraudulent.
The proportion of actually positive cases that the model correctly classified as positive. In fraud detection, check it to reduce missed fraudulent transactions.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall. Because the value decreases when either metric is low, it is used to compare the two metrics together.

A family of evaluation metrics that measures matching words and word order by comparing a generated summary with a reference summary. Other evaluations are also used to verify factual accuracy and important conditions.
Running a model on representative and failure-prone inputs to verify the accuracy, safety, speed, and other qualities required for its use. Multiple models are compared under the same conditions.
The practice of considering AI’s impact on users and society, and evaluating and addressing fairness, explainability, privacy, safety, and other concerns from design through operation.
A systematic skew in a model’s results for a particular group caused by factors such as training data or design. Results are compared using data representative of the intended use.
The property that allows users and operators to understand why a model produced a result and what information influenced it. The scope of explanations is defined according to the use case.

An evaluation that divides subjects by factors such as speaking style or usage conditions and compares each group’s performance and errors. It can reveal differences that are difficult to see in the overall average.
A state in which a model learns patterns specific to its training data and cannot perform well enough on unseen data. Performance is checked using data separate from the training data.

A state in which a model fails to learn the patterns needed for the task sufficiently and makes many errors on both training and validation data. The data, model, and training conditions are reviewed.

A document summarizing a model’s intended uses, performance evaluations, limitations, and risks. For example, before introducing a model into a new business process, its evaluation conditions and scope of applicability are reviewed.

Operating AI by defining its purposes, the models and data that may be used, approval and audit procedures, and responsible owners. Responses to changes and issues are recorded, and policies are reviewed.

The principle of collecting, transmitting, and storing only the data needed for processing. For example, when asking generative AI to summarize a consultation, an unnecessary customer number is removed from the input.

A record used to verify later who performed what action on which target, when, and with what result. The fields to store, retention period, and access permissions are defined according to the audit purpose.

A feature that allows load balancer nodes to distribute traffic to targets in enabled zones other than their own Availability Zone. With an Application Load Balancer, it can be disabled per target group.

A resource-based policy configured for an S3 bucket. It specifies who can perform which actions on the bucket or its objects, and under what conditions. For example, you can allow files to be retrieved only when requests pass through a specific VPC endpoint.

A unit that groups the destinations to which a load balancer forwards requests. In an Application Load Balancer, you configure the registered targets, the protocol and port used for communication, health checks, and other settings for each group.

A mechanism that keeps sending a user’s subsequent requests to the same destination. An Application Load Balancer uses cookies to maintain routing to the same target group or target, depending on the configuration.

A setting in a single Application Load Balancer forwarding rule that distributes requests among multiple target groups according to assigned weights. For example, setting the old version to 95 and the new version to 5 reduces the proportion of requests assigned to the new version.

The property that allows applications running the required versions to read and write data correctly even when its structure or value types change. While new and old applications share a database, verify that both can read back and update rows written by either version.
A service that provides fixed entry-point IP addresses and sends TCP or UDP traffic through the AWS global network to healthy endpoints. You can manage entry points and health by Region.

A method that changes the destination returned by DNS to a standby destination based on operating status. The timing of client switching is affected by when a new name lookup occurs, DNS caching, and similar factors.

A Route 53 VPC Resolver connection point that accepts DNS queries directed to a VPC from on-premises DNS servers and similar sources. It is used for tasks such as resolving names in private hosted zones associated with the VPC.

A Route 53 VPC Resolver connection point for forwarding DNS queries from a VPC to on-premises DNS servers and similar destinations. Forwarding rules specify the target domains and forwarding destinations.
A configuration that sends only queries for specific domain names to designated DNS servers. For example, it can be used when querying AWS private names from a corporate DNS server.
The source from which CloudFront retrieves content. You configure an S3 bucket, load balancer, or similar resource to determine the path for retrieving uncached data and the access permissions.

The network on the site or data-center side used by a company or similar organization. When connecting it to AWS, both sides agree on the address ranges, name resolution, and the scope of permitted traffic.

A unit that connects a network such as a VPC or VPN to a Transit Gateway. You can configure route tables that process traffic received from the attachment and route tables to which routes are propagated.
A list of routes that Transit Gateway consults to determine where to forward packets received from an attachment. You can choose the list referenced by each attachment.
A configuration that specifies which route table processes packets entering Transit Gateway from a given attachment. Changing the association may change the route selected for the same destination.

A configuration that reflects the route information held by an attachment in a selected Transit Gateway route table. To allow bidirectional communication, verify the routes in the tables referenced for both the outbound and return paths.
A VPC that collects traffic from other networks for firewall inspection. Routes such as Transit Gateway paths are arranged so requests and responses pass through the intended inspection points.

A setting in which a Transit Gateway attachment in an inspection VPC keeps the Availability Zone used by the same traffic flow. Routes must also ensure that both requests and responses pass through the stateful firewall.
An AWS service that inspects and controls network traffic traversing VPC routes using rules. Direct the route for the traffic to be inspected to a firewall endpoint.

A destination in a VPC that passes packets to AWS Network Firewall for traffic inspection. Configure it in the route table; when stateful inspection is required, send requests and responses through the same inspection path.

The path taken by response packets from the destination back to the original source. Check the response-side routes and communication permissions as well as those on the sending side. With a stateful firewall, also verify the inspection points used in both directions.

The maximum packet size that can be sent over a single network connection. If an outgoing packet exceeds the size supported by an intermediate connection, fragmentation or sender-side size adjustment may be required.

The largest packet size that can traverse the entire path from source to destination without fragmentation. It is determined by the smallest MTU along the path, so it can indicate why short communications succeed while larger ones stop.

A feature that analyzes whether a specified source and destination can communicate with the current AWS network configuration. It can identify the resources traversed and the points of blockage without generating actual traffic.

A feature that records information about IP traffic passing through network interfaces in a VPC. Use it to check sources, destinations, ports, and whether traffic was allowed or rejected when investigating communications.

An organized view of the data and systems to protect, the threats considered, communication boundaries, and required safeguards. During design, it helps compare who can access resources and through which paths.
A log that records information about requests received by an Application Load Balancer. It shows timestamps and request results and helps investigate application problems and traffic trends.

An intermediary that connects to external services on behalf of users or applications. You can configure which destinations are allowed and record connection dates and times and destinations according to your organization’s requirements.

A suite of protocols that encrypts IP communications and verifies the identity of the communication peer and the integrity of the data. AWS Site-to-Site VPN uses IPsec to protect the connection between an on-premises site and AWS.

A mechanism that digitally signs DNS records and verifies that DNS responses come from the correct published source and have not been tampered with. Application data is protected using TLS or similar technologies.
A setting that restricts public access to S3. When enabled for an account or bucket, it can restrict public access even if settings allowing public access are later added.

A mechanism that temporarily stores processing requests so the execution side can retrieve them when ready. For example, sending an image-conversion request to Amazon SQS separates conversion processing from the registration screen.

In Amazon SQS, the period during which a received message is temporarily hidden from other processing workers. If processing is not completed and the message is not deleted during this period, it may become available again.
Switching processing or communication to a standby system when a failure occurs. For example, with an RDS Multi-AZ deployment, another AZ takes over database processing during a failure.
A mechanism that delivers content from an edge location close to the user. For example, when CloudFront has cached a response, it can return it to the user without retrieving it from the origin.

The proportion of requests served with a cached response among requests that consult the cache. Checking this value in CloudFront shows how many requests were answered without being sent back to the origin.

An operation that invalidates responses stored in the cache so that, when the same content is requested next, it can be retrieved again from the origin. In CloudFront, you can specify the paths to target.

A CloudWatch metric that records the time from when an Application Load Balancer sends a request to a target until that target begins sending response headers. Comparing it with the total response time measured on the user side helps identify where waiting time increased.

The amount of work that can be processed in a given period. For example, an order API may use the number of requests processed per second and combine it with the time taken by individual requests to assess performance.
A setting that moves Amazon S3 objects to different storage classes or expires them based on conditions such as elapsed days. Define rules after checking retention obligations and retrieval times.
A logical environment for calling a deployed API in API Gateway. Each stage can have separate URLs, settings, log output, and other configurations.
A specification agreed on by callers and implementers covering an API’s inputs, outputs, errors, authentication, and more. When changing it, check compatibility and the impact on users.
AWS CDK is a development framework for defining cloud infrastructure in a programming language and deploying it as CloudFormation templates.
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is an in-memory cache compatible with DynamoDB, used to reduce read load and latency.
Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) is a managed registry for storing, managing, and deploying container images.

The process of removing or replacing sensitive portions, such as personal information and authentication tokens, from values displayed in logs or on screens. Separate identifiers needed for investigation from sensitive values.
AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) is a framework for defining serverless application resources concisely and deploying them with CloudFormation.
The AWS SDK’s retry behavior. When SDK and application retries are layered, check the retry count, wait time, and idempotency to avoid excessive calls.
The behavior of limiting requests to prevent excessive service demand. When it occurs, check quotas, concurrency, and retry intervals to adjust the load.

An association that lets Lambda poll an event source such as Amazon SQS and invoke a function with batches of retrieved messages. Check event retrieval, batching, and failure handling separately from the function code.
A method of gradually increasing the interval between retries after temporary failures. Design it with limits and jitter so requests do not concentrate on a failing dependency within a short time.
An operation that retrieves items in DynamoDB by specifying a partition key and, when needed, sort-key conditions. Designing keys to match access patterns helps avoid scanning all items.
An operation that reads all items in a DynamoDB table or index. Because a filter is applied only after reading, consider Query for requirements that can be narrowed by key.

A URL that permits a specific operation on an S3 object only during the signed URL’s validity period. Because anyone who knows the URL can access it, limit its expiration, operation, and distribution.
An AWS Systems Manager capability for storing and retrieving configuration values and secrets as parameters. Protect sensitive values by combining SecureString, KMS, and access permissions.

An AWS Systems Manager application configuration management capability. It separates configuration profiles from environments and safely delivers application configurations using validation and deployment strategies.
A named pointer to a specific version of a Lambda function. It links environments or release targets to versions and supports progressive deployments, including traffic splitting.

A method of recording request IDs, timestamps, processing stages, results, and error types using consistent field names and formats. Separate identifiers used for searching and aggregation from sensitive values that must not be output.
An identifier that correlates logs, events, and traces originating from the same user request. It enables investigation across services without putting the sensitive value itself in logs.

The number of processes that can run at the same time. Increasing Lambda concurrency can also increase connections to and calls to downstream services, so adjust it together with connection counts, quotas, and error rates.
A mechanism that adjusts compute capacity based on demand and health checks. Define minimum and maximum capacity, scaling conditions, and launchable configurations to meet operational requirements.

An AWS Systems Manager feature that automates operational tasks such as maintenance, deployment, and remediation. Clearly define the targets, permissions, inputs, stop conditions, and results in the operating procedure.
An operational document that defines procedures for incidents and routine operations, including targets, pre-checks, execution permissions, success criteria, stop conditions, and rollback.
A diff used before updating a CloudFormation stack to review the resources that will be created, changed, or deleted. It helps identify unintended replacements or deletions before approval.
The AWS-side connection point for a VPN attached to a VPC. For example, a subnet route table can forward traffic destined for the corporate network to the virtual private gateway.

A record about a potential security issue generated by a threat detection service or similar system. Do not assume the cause; verify the affected resource, time, and related evidence before deciding how to respond.
A CloudTrail configuration that collects AWS activity records and can deliver events to Amazon S3, CloudWatch Logs, or EventBridge.
A CloudTrail event representing a management operation on a resource in an AWS account. It provides evidence for investigating who performed which operation and when.
A design for preserving the logs and records required for investigation, auditing, and recovery, together with their retention period, encryption, and access permissions.
